title: Grade 5 Math — Wed, Jun 18
description: Data Handling — Day 3 of 5: Bar graphs — reading and drawing
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A bar graph uses:
options: Rectangular bars of different heights to represent data
questions.explanation: A bar graph uses rectangular bars. The height (or length) of each bar represents the value/frequency of each category.

questions.question: In a bar graph, the horizontal axis (x-axis) usually shows:
questions.explanation: The x-axis (horizontal) shows the categories. The y-axis (vertical) shows the values/frequency.

questions.question: In a bar graph, the vertical axis (y-axis) shows:
questions.explanation: The y-axis shows the scale of values (numbers). Each bar's height corresponds to a value on the y-axis.

questions.question: Bar graph — Favourite subjects: Maths=30, Science=25, Hindi=20, English=15. Which has the tallest bar?
questions.explanation: Maths has the highest value (30) → tallest bar.

questions.question: Same bar graph (Maths=30, Science=25, Hindi=20, English=15). How many more students prefer Maths than English?
Same graph (Maths=30, Science=25, Hindi=20, English=15). What is the total number of students surveyed?
The scale of a bar graph is set at 0, 5, 10, 15... A bar reaches the 25 mark. The value is:
questions.explanation: The bar reaches the 25 mark → value = 25.

questions.question: A bar graph shows monthly rainfall (mm): Jan=20, Feb=30, Mar=50, Apr=80. Which month had the highest rainfall?
questions.explanation: April = 80 mm → highest bar → most rainfall.

questions.question: Monthly rainfall (Jan=20, Feb=30, Mar=50, Apr=80). What was the total rainfall for these 4 months?
What is the FIRST step when drawing a bar graph?
options: Write the title and label the axes
questions.explanation: Step 1: Draw and label the axes. Step 2: Choose an appropriate scale. Step 3: Draw bars to the correct height. Step 4: Write the title.

questions.question: When choosing the scale for a bar graph with values 15, 30, 45, 60 — a good scale interval is:
questions.explanation: A scale of 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 (intervals of 15) works perfectly. Or 0, 10, 20... would also work. Scale should divide data cleanly.

questions.question: A double bar graph shows two sets of data side by side. What is its advantage?
options: It allows easy comparison between two groups for each category
It does not need a title
questions.explanation: A double bar graph compares two datasets (e.g. boys vs girls, this year vs last year) for the same categories side by side.

questions.question: In a bar graph, the bars should:
options: Have gaps between them (to show they are separate categories)
questions.explanation: In a standard bar graph, there are gaps between bars to show they represent separate categories. (Histograms have no gaps, but that is for continuous data.)
